issues.description: The supplied programs contain author-machine paths and Startup File includes; the ordered cross-language handoffs, active macros and input roots need a project working-copy setup.

The supplied LCA branch requires PROC LCA plus LCA_Distal_BCH_v110.sas, LCAGraphicsV2.sas and the invoked winsorization macro; their availability and the supported installation/field contract have not been verified. The paper-wide general estimation/tabulation code omitted from the release is contextual and outside this supplied-code target.

The SAS producer exports ten positional columns without names; CheckEPS_CC.py reads filename, GAAP EPS and non-GAAP EPS from indices 3/8/7, and emits six columns without fileLength although its SAS consumer reads seven fields including fileLength. Correct the indices and output field contract in a working copy before this branch can be used.

Assembling Final Dataset.sas and LCA Analyses.sas consume promin.externaldata2, but the supplied Gathering Other Data.sas creates promin.externaldata. Its required field aliases also remain unproven: LCA keeps ff10, calyear_1 and MEETBEAT while the supplied producer visibly creates FF48, calyear/eayear and does not visibly create MEETBEAT. Do not infer a rename or fill the handoff without a source contract.

DownloadFilings.py writes exhibit_id_errors.txt only in the multiple-exhibits branch, while Process Prominence Output from Python_v1.6.sas imports the file unconditionally. A clean per-run working directory must ensure a zero-row-compatible log exists before the SAS import; stale logs must not be reused.

The observed Python 3.12.14 runtime uses urllib.request, while DownloadFilings.py imports urllib2 and relies on byte strings in regex/text-file processing. A compatible Python 2 runtime was not established; if retaining Python 3, the URL import and decoding/text I/O contract need a supported source update.

The currently configured SAS executable fails an empty-session launch at TKELS initialization, preventing a run in this environment. This probe does not establish a missing license; the runtime launch configuration/component must be resolved before future execution.

evidence.quote:
2. “Setup for SA CC Data Parsing in Python.sas”
This SAS code links firm-quarter observations to conference call transcript data. The conference call transcripts were originally scraped from SeekingAlpha.com and were made available to Kurt Gee while at Stanford University. 
3. “DownloadFilings.py”
This Python script takes as an input the data from Step 1 and downloads the 8-K filings in their raw, unprocessed form as .txt files.
4. “CheckEPS.py”
This Python script takes as an input the list of files from Step 1 and the directory of filings from Step 3 and searches, separately, for the positions of non-GAAP EPS and GAAP EPS. This step outputs all instances of the EPS numbers in each filing, as well as the position of each instance.
5. “CheckEPS_CC.py”
This Python script performs a similar task as Step 4 but using the sample of Conference Call Transcripts.
6. “Process Prominence Output from Python_v1.6.sas”`
This SAS code takes as an input the results of previous steps and outputs a SAS dataset with information on the prominence of non-GAAP EPS and GAAP EPS in both the earnings announcement and the conference call.
The variable NG_FIRST that we use in the paper, both the earnings announcement version and the conference call version (NG_FIRST_CC), is available at https://sites.google.com/view/kurthgee/data for access and use. Thus, readers can simply download the data directly rather than gathering all the underlying sources of information to construct the measure based on this documentation and our code.

			exhibits=re.findall('<DOCUMENT>(?:.(?<!<TYPE>))*?<TYPE>EX-99.*?</DOCUMENT>',text,flags=re.I | re.S) # allows for EX-99, EX-99.1, or EX-99.2

			elif (len(exhibits)==0):
				EA_text = text
				f=open(directory + filename, 'w')
				f.write(EA_text)
			
			# If multiple exhibits, rule out exhibits with conference call transcripts and extract the rest
			else:
			
				## Identify and remove Conference Calls
				# Search for "conference call", "teleconference", or "webcast" (ignoring case) in the first 2000 characters, return the entire document
				documents=re.findall('<DOCUMENT>.{0,2000}?(?:conference call|conference-call|teleconference|tele-conference|webcast|web-cast).*?</DOCUMENT>',text,flags=re.I | re.S)
				
				# Process each potential conference call document
				for doc in documents:
				
					# If "conference call" or "teleconference" or "webcast" is in the description of the document, then replace the entire document with a space
					if re.search('<DESCRIPTION>[^<]{0,2000}?(conference call|conference-call|teleconference|tele-conference|webcast|web-cast)[^<]*?<|',str(doc),flags=re.I) is not None:
						text=text.replace(doc, ' ')
					
					# If the word "transcript" is in the text of the document, then replace the entire document with a space
					elif 'transcript' in doc:
						text=text.replace(doc, ' ')
				
				# Extract the rest of the text
				EA_text = text
				f=open(directory + filename, 'w')
				f.write(EA_text)
				
				# Note the filing in a log file to reference later
				h=open('exhibit_id_errors.txt', 'a')
				h.write(filename+','+corpusdict[filename]['url']+','+directory+','+str(len(exhibits))+'\n')
				h.close()
